faq.title: Frequently asked questions about World Monitor Pro
faq.a1: Yes. The core platform remains free. Pro adds equity research, macro analytics, and AI briefings. Pro Business adds the commercial license and data export. Enterprise adds team deployments and TV apps.
faq.a2: Pro is for investors, analysts, and professionals who want stock monitoring, geopolitical analysis, economy analytics, and AI-powered daily briefings — all under one key.
faq.a3: Enterprise is for teams that need shared use, APIs, integrations, deployment options, and direct support.
faq.q4: Can I start with Pro and upgrade later?
faq.a4: Yes. Pro is for personal use. Pro Business ($49.99/mo) adds the commercial license, data export, 25 dashboards, and 250 MCP calls/day. API plans cover programmatic access, and Enterprise covers custom deployments. To move from Pro to Pro Business, choose Pro Business while signed in: your subscription switches over, you see today's charge before you confirm, and your billing period restarts that day.
faq.q5: Is this only for conflict monitoring?
faq.a5: No. World Monitor is primarily a global intelligence platform covering stock markets, macroeconomics, geopolitical analysis, energy, infrastructure, and more. Conflict tracking is one of many capabilities — not the focus.
faq.q6: Why keep the core platform free?
faq.a6: Because public access matters. Paid plans fund deeper workflows for serious users and organizations.
faq.q7: Can I still use my own API keys?
faq.a7: Yes. Bring-your-own-keys always works. Pro simply means you don't have to register for separate services.
faq.a8: MCP lets AI agents — Claude, GPT, custom LLMs — use World Monitor as a tool, querying registered services. Included in Pro. Enterprise adds private MCP servers and custom deployments.
faq.q9: Can I build my own panels?
faq.a9: Yes. Pro includes the Custom Widget Builder — build panels from HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with AI-assisted modification.
faq.q10: Can I connect Claude or GPT to World Monitor?
faq.a10: Yes. MCP is included in Pro — plug World Monitor into Claude, GPT, or any MCP-compatible LLM as a live tool.
faq.a11: Pick your cadence — daily, twice-daily, or weekly. We re-score every tracked story against your alert rules and watchlist, dedupe across sources, and send up to 30 ranked items with an AI Assessment and Signals to watch written to your context. Real-time alerts are also available for critical events.
faq.a12: Pro refreshes market quotes every 30 seconds. Other datasets follow each source's own cadence. Free stays on the standard source cadence.
faq.a13: Notification channels are AES-256 encrypted at rest. Digests never leave our pipeline unredacted.

moments.title: How does World Monitor correlate signals?

m1.s2: Ships, chokepoints, flights, cables and infrastructure proximity show whether that pressure can hit supply, trade or capital routes.
m1.s3: Rates, FX, equities, crypto, energy and safe-haven assets show which market regime is repricing.
m1.s4: The edge is seeing geopolitical pressure, transmission path and price action together before it becomes a consensus note.

m2.s3: Oil, gas, gold, grains, miners, shipping names and commodity-linked currencies show how the shock prices through.

m3.s1: {{aiDatacenters}} AI datacenters sit beside grids, pipelines, LNG, nuclear facilities, cloud regions and power-market exposure.
m3.s2: Grid stress, outages, heat, fire and weather layers show which compute corridors are under pressure today.

depth.title: How deep is the World Monitor data model?
depth.sub: Every number below is live in the dashboard today — not a roadmap.
depth.n1Desc: Live orbital positions computed in-browser with SGP4 and updated every 3 seconds — military and Earth-observation satellites from CelesTrak, refreshed every 2 hours.
depth.n2Desc: Daily RF-interference map from aircraft reports: cells where at least 2% of aircraft see degraded GPS are flagged, over 10% marked high. The cells are hexagons rebuilt once a day from those reports, so the map shows where flights met jamming or spoofing over the latest day, not this minute.
depth.n3Desc: Vessel counts through Hormuz, Suez, Bab el-Mandeb and 10 more straits — with disruption scoring.
depth.n4Desc: {{aiDatacenters}} AI datacenters mapped with power and operator metadata — the physical layer of the AI race.
depth.n5Desc: {{submarineCables}} undersea cables that carry the internet, overlaid with outage and threat signals.
depth.n6Desc: Protest detection from ACLED and GDELT; reports from one source in the same 0.1° cell on the same day merge into one event — signal, not rumor.

faq.title: What are common questions about World Monitor?
faq.sub: {{answers}} straight answers on price, data, alerts and AI access. The short version: the dashboard costs $0, needs no account, and the code is open source under AGPL-3.0.
faq.a1: Yes. The live map costs $0 with no signup and no trial clock: {{mapLayers}} map layer types, every one but Resilience, plus curated feeds, country briefs, breaking alerts and monitoring surfaces. Pro pays for the feeds: it adds WM Analyst, the scenario engine, Route Explorer, scheduled digests, MCP access for AI clients and the Resilience map layer. No ads, and no account means there's no user data to sell.
faq.q2: What is a global intelligence dashboard?
faq.a2: A single live view that fuses signals most tools keep separate: conflict events, ship and aircraft tracking, shipping chokepoints, satellites, subsea cables, pipelines, markets and cyber threats — on one real-time world map, with AI scoring and briefs on top. World Monitor is a free one.
faq.q3: Where does the data come from?
faq.a3: From {{providers}} attributed providers. Named ones include ACLED and UCDP for conflict, AISStream for live vessels, OpenSky for aircraft, NASA FIRMS for fires, USGS for earthquakes, IMF, BIS, FRED and Finnhub for markets and macro — plus curated news feeds. Every panel cites its sources and timestamps inline.
faq.q4: Can I watch chokepoints like Hormuz or Bab el-Mandeb in real time?
faq.a4: Yes. {{chokepoints}} chokepoints, both straits and canals, from Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb to Suez, are tracked with live AIS vessel counts, week-over-week transit change and disruption scoring — and density anomalies are flagged against each chokepoint's rolling baseline.
faq.q5: How is this different from a conflict map like Liveuamap?
faq.a5: Conflict is one map layer. World Monitor fuses conflicts with shipping, military flights, infrastructure, markets and cyber — then AI scores the convergence: instability indices, hotspot escalation, corroborated breaking alerts and daily briefs. Compare World Monitor with Liveuamap and other conflict maps: worldmonitor.app/compare/liveuamap-alternatives. For broader monitoring options, see worldmonitor.app/compare/best-geopolitical-risk-dashboards.
faq.q6: Why should I trust an alert?
faq.a6: Because a banner has to clear fixed gates. It fires for news items classified as a critical or high threat, and for official civil-defense sirens. A news alert must be under 15 minutes old, the same story is held back for 30 minutes, and a 60-second cooldown follows any alert unless the new one is more severe. Keyword-only matches from lower-tier outlets also need AI confirmation. Sirens skip the age and cooldown gates because they are time-critical.
faq.q7: Can AI agents like Claude or GPT use it?
faq.a7: Yes. World Monitor's MCP server exposes {{mcpTools}} live tools, so Claude, GPT or any MCP-compatible agent can query risk scores, chokepoint status, conflicts, markets and briefs — with JMESPath projection so agents fetch exactly what they need.
faq.a8: No. The dashboard works instantly with no signup. An account only matters when you upgrade to Pro or want settings synced across devices.
faq.a9: Yes — open source under AGPL-3.0 on GitHub: read the code, self-host it, or build on it. Pro and Pro Business include desktop keys, so your own desktop build can load Pro cloud data; Docker copies run on their own data. Native desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux are available too, plus an Android TV app for wall displays under an Enterprise contract.
faq.a10: Palantir makes an institution's own data operational inside that institution. World Monitor starts from the other end: it assembles, normalizes, correlates, and monitors public-world data, then publishes that intelligence layer through a free dashboard and open-source code. Different job, different product.
faq.q11: Which World Monitor license do I need?
faq.a11: Choose based on who will use the output. Pro's Personal license is for one person using World Monitor for their own research and decisions. Pro Business lets one licensed user use it for company or client work, internal tools, and reports. API Starter covers API use inside one organization, with no customer redistribution. API Business lets that organization embed World Monitor data in products and services for its customers. Enterprise covers custom seats, white-labeling, and deployments. These subscription licenses are separate from the AGPL/MIT source-code licenses. Full terms: worldmonitor.app/docs/terms.
faq.q12: What is the best software for tracking global news disruptions?
faq.a12: World Monitor is a free, open-source option: it streams {{feeds}} news and OSINT feeds from {{providers}} attributed providers onto one live world map with {{mapLayers}} map layer types, spanning geopolitics, markets, shipping, aviation and cyber. It correlates them so converging disruptions surface before the headlines do. To weigh it against other tools, see worldmonitor.app/compare/best-geopolitical-risk-dashboards.
